facts.text: Guido of Arezzo was an eleventh-century Benedictine monk and music theorist, born sometime in the 990s and still alive in 1033.
Guido lived at the monastery of Pomposa in northern Italy and later moved to Arezzo, where he trained the cathedral's singers.
Before Guido, church singers learned chants mostly by ear and memory and could spend many years memorizing the chants for the church year.
The older written signs, called neumes, showed whether a melody went up or down but not exactly how far.
Guido is credited with the musical staff: pitches were placed on and between lines, so singers could see the exact pitch of each note.
He used a Latin hymn to Saint John the Baptist, Ut queant laxis; each of its first six lines begins one step higher than the line before.
Taking the first syllable of each of those six lines gave the note names ut, re, mi, fa, sol and la.
With the syllables, a singer could link the notes of a new chant to the pattern of a tune he already knew; mi to fa always marked the half step.
The words of the hymn were known long before Guido; it is uncertain whether he wrote its tune or used an existing one.
Pope John XIX, who led the Church from 1024 to 1033, asked Guido three times to come to Rome and show his teaching method.
In Rome the pope was delighted with the method and did not let Guido leave until he himself could sing a melody he had never heard before.
In the 1600s (the 17th century), the Italian scholar Giovanni Battista Doni proposed replacing ut with do, an open syllable that is easier to sing.
A seventh syllable, si, was added later, probably from the first letters of Sancte Ioannes, the last words of the hymn; it is also sung as ti.
In the 1800s (the 19th century), Sarah Glover suggested replacing si so that each syllable would start with a different letter.
The Guidonian hand, a memory aid that places note syllables on the joints of the hand, bears his name but was probably developed by later teachers.
Music students still use these syllables today when they learn to sing scales and read music at sight.

notes: Guido 的出生地各來源不同（s2 說可能生於法國，s4 稱義大利理論家）；選文只寫他在義大利的修道院與 Arezzo 工作。教宗的年份 1024–1033 是在位期間
